rationale: The source contains no seven-day check and preserves only a zero-day NEW classification, so a missing deadline classification rule is plausible. However, clause 65(8) requires updating CKYCR records. The program only displays a status and provides no evidence of transmission, completion, or the relationship between its elapsed-day input and receipt of updated customer information. The proposed OK/LATE interface is not established by the source. The intended behavior therefore exceeds what the source and fixtures can demonstrate.
scope_judgment: Lines 22–26 are blank lines inside 2000-CHECK-SLA and can accommodate a local classification rule while preserving the existing zero-day override. This scope cannot establish actual CKYCR updates or receipt-date provenance. Revise the intended behavior to a justified deadline-status classification or supply evidence supporting the broader obligation.
intended_fixture_judgment: The eight-day fixture tests the first day beyond the inclusive seven-day limit, and the seven-day regression fixture supplies the complementary boundary. These are useful finite classification tests, but expected LATE and OK values are proposed conventions rather than source-established requirements. Neither output proves a CKYCR update occurred within seven days. Support the interface and input semantics before accepting these expectations.
regression_fixture_judgment: The zero-day NEW expectation is grounded in the unchanged source and tests its override after any restored rule. The one-day and seven-day OK expectations are new intended behavior, not existing valid outcomes: the frozen source leaves WS-SLA-STATUS unchanged for both inputs. Reclassify those fixtures accordingly. The outside-locus fixture observes only one status outcome and does not establish comprehensive preservation of behavior outside the edit scope.
capability_judgment: The packet reports an available GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 batch backend with no compiler error, but case_checks_executed is false. Compilation and execution may validate the supplied finite status fixtures once a candidate exists; no checks currently pass. The backend expressly lacks complete semantic-equivalence proof, and these fixtures cannot validate CKYCR transmission or regulatory compliance.
duplicate_source_judgment: Preselection before detector results, retention of source-bundle dependence, disclosure of both case and distinct-bundle counts, and avoidance of independent-case interval claims provide a defensible conditional justification for repeated sources. Retention remains contingent on reviewer approval and continued dependent-group reporting. This single packet does not independently verify preselection or other members of the group.
unresolved_issues: The intended regulatory-compliance claim is unsupported by a status-only program and fixtures.
The OK/LATE status convention and receipt-based elapsed-day semantics require justification.
The one-day and seven-day fixtures must be identified as intended behavior rather than preservation of frozen-source outcomes.
No candidate compilation or case execution results are supplied.
